text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government wants to solve recurring fuel shortage "once and for all" when task force on petrol meets in Abuja on Thursday, says Haruna Abubakar, chief executive of PPMC, the state oil arm responsible for fuel supplies and distribution.
- Passenger train derails near eastern city of Port Harcourt; no casualty and no damage to the train.
- Anxious loan applicants under family economic advancement programme have innudated government offices with enquiries on when exactly the programme launched in March will comence.
- Stock exchange deputy chief Ndi Okereke-Onyuike calls on federal government to abolish capital gains tax and stamp duty on share transactions.

- Nigeria's defence headquarters dismisses alleged capture of its troops in Sierra Leone during fighting in Freetown on Monday and alleges that soldiers who seized power in Sierra Leone looted the central bank.
- Aviation minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh blames lackadaisical attitude of Nigeria Airways staff for ban on Nigerian planes by Britain.
- Government revokes allocation of undeveloped plots in capital Abuja, which will now be passed onto to more serious developers, officials say.
- West African force ECOMOG prepares for fresh attack on Freetown to force soldiers to restore to power democratically elected president deposed last month.
- Banks lead private sector in the movement to Abuja as they rush to open offices in the new capital.
- Nigeria and China agree to set up firms in export processing zone in southeast whose products will be exported to China to reduce the imbalance in their bilateral trade.
